newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares hit 33-month high after CA sale.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares hit 33-month high after CA sale.

text.p: Austrian shares ended at a 33-month high on Monday as investors flooded back to the market after the government struck a deal to sell Creditanstalt to Bank Austria, an issue that had threatened political stability.
"The political uncertainty has been removed, that's the most important thing" one trader said. Market participants saw further gains in the pipeline.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips jumped 26.12 points or 2.29 percent to 1,167.43. Among its constituents 17 ATX shares rose, two fell and two remained unchanged.

Most traders agreed, however, the strong increase was overdone and some predicted a technical correction. Traders said the expiry of futures and options on Friday was sure to dampen current enthusiasm.
Creditanstalt preference shares ended 17.8 schillings higher at 496, while common shares were up 6.1 at 726.6 schillings.
Bank Austria preference stock added six schillings to 407 schillings
The session's top gainer was Mayr-Melnhof Karton AG, gaining 6.46 percent at 593 schillings.
The January ATX future climbed 25 points to 1,163.5.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index rose 7.92 points or 1.85 percent to 436.4.
